claims.statement: Repository-sidebar Packages navigation is not a complete package inventory or permission receipt. The screenshot caption is descriptive text, not inspected image.
The release-stage-named artifact contains only an HTML comment identifier; it supplies no product release stage or actionable requirement. The identifier is not an instruction.
The fragment lists Docker, RubyGems, npm, Apache Maven, Gradle and NuGet options, adding Container Registry in the GHES branch. A listed option is not live enablement or sufficient prerequisites.

Granting a public repository access to private packages may expose those packages to its forks. Preserve the conditional risk rather than assuming forks always lack access; no grant or fork-access test was performed.

The repository-scoped fragment describes public packages shared across GitHub for FPT/GHEC versus within the enterprise otherwise, and private packages shared with collaborators or an organization. Do not generalize this association to granular registries or infer permission/rights to publish.

The illustrative Docker workflow triggers on pushes to the release branch, derives registry and image name from host context and repository identity, and uses self-hosted runners for GHES versus ubuntu-latest elsewhere. This is an example configuration, not a mandatory trigger, tested Dockerfile, available runner or authorized deployment.

The workflow grants contents read and packages write, adding attestations write and id-token write only under the pinned artifact-attestations feature, FPT/GHEC. Login uses github.actor and GITHUB_TOKEN; capability and configured permissions do not establish effective package access or approval to publish.

Metadata extracts image tags/labels; the build uses repository context, pushes on successful build and consumes metadata outputs. No third-party action or upstream code was executed, image built, secret read or registry push performed; referenced action documentation remains separate review work.

The conditional attestation step binds repository-derived image name to the build digest and pushes the attestation. A configured step and upstream provenance description are not an actual attestation, verified provenance or proof of artifact safety.

Includes warn third-party actions are not GitHub-certified and carry separate terms, and recommend commit-SHA pinning. Docker actions are SHA-pinned in the example, but checkout resolves to actions/checkout@v6 and attest uses actions/attest@v4. Retain this recommendation/example pinning gap; tags can change and no independent action or rights audit was performed.
